title: sync
description: One sync run: what it re-listed, what it stored, and why it stopped. Since #232 this is the only command that pulls data from Strava — it drains missing streams paced against Strava's limits and stops on the per-run read budget, so a first run on a fresh install may need repeating. Read `resumable` to decide.

streams_fetched.description: stream rows STORED this run. Not reads spent: a read whose body will not decode stores nothing and is counted in streams_skipped, and a 404 stores an empty marker rather than streams

streams_skipped.description: reads whose body would not decode as UTF-8. Nothing was stored, so these stay pending and retry next run. A value that repeats across runs means the data is unreadable rather than merely late

pending_streams.description: activities still without any streams row after this run. An activity Strava has no streams for does NOT count: its 404 stores an empty marker, which retires it permanently

stopped.description: Why the run ended. `complete` = the stream queue emptied; `budget_reached` = the run filled Strava's 15-minute read window; `rate_limited` = Strava returned 429 on a STREAM read; `list_rate_limited` = Strava returned 429 on the ACTIVITY LIST, so the listing is incomplete and nothing was pruned (#235). The last two are the same upstream condition and have the same remedy — run again in ~15 minutes — but they are distinct values because they describe different incomplete states, and a drain that 429s on its first id is otherwise indistinguishable from a list that 429s on page one. All four arrive in a SUCCESS envelope at exit 0. Do not discriminate on this token against the `rate_limited` ERROR code, which is a different thing in a different envelope shape — discriminate on the envelope.

resumable.description: Whether anything is still missing, so the run should be repeated. Usually `pending_streams > 0`, re-measured from the database in every arm. It is also true when `stopped` is `list_rate_limited` even with an empty queue, because what was left undone there is the LISTING, not the stream backlog — a run refused on page one has nothing pending and absolutely must be repeated.
